record.paper_title: Autonomous Agents Modelling Other Agents: A Comprehensive Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can one design efficient methods for modelling other agents in open multiagent systems, where agents may enter and leave the system at arbitrary times without notifying others, the number of agents is not fixed, and knowledge from past systems may need to be transferred into new ones?

evidence.quote: In contrast to open multiagent systems, in which agents may enter and leave the system at any time during the interaction, without necessarily notifying other agents.

While some works investigated modelling other agents in open multiagent systems (Chandrasekaran et al., 2016; Huynh et al., 2006; Rovatsos et al., 2003), it remains a significant open challenge to develop efficient modelling methods for such systems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an open multiagent system defined as follows. Time proceeds in discrete steps t = 0, 1, 2, .... At each time t there is a finite set of agents A_t, and the cardinality |A_t| is not fixed in advance: agents may enter or leave A_t at arbitrary times without announcing their arrival or departure to the remaining agents. Each agent i ∈ A_t selects actions according to an unknown (possibly time-varying) policy π_i, and a designated modelling agent m observes only a sequence of joint observations and actions of those agents currently present.

A modelling method for agent m is an algorithm that, at each time t, maintains for every other agent j ∈ A_t \ {m} a predictive model π̂_j of that agent's behaviour, using only the history of observations available to m up to time t. The modelling method must additionally support transfer: knowledge accumulated about agents encountered in past systems (S_1, S_2, ..., S_k) may be reused to bootstrap models in a new system S_{k+1} whose agent population is unknown and possibly disjoint.

Design such a modelling method that is efficient in the following senses simultaneously:
  (i) its per-step computational and memory cost scales sublinearly in the cumulative number of agents ever encountered;
  (ii) its predictive accuracy, measured by the expected loss between π̂_j and π_j on observed actions, converges (in an appropriate sense) for every agent j who remains in the system long enough; and
  (iii) it correctly handles the entry of previously unseen agents and the departure of agents without prior notification, without catastrophic degradation of the models maintained for the remaining agents.

Provide either a constructive algorithm with provable guarantees of (i)–(iii), or prove an impossibility result delineating the limits of what any such modelling method can achieve.
artifact.status_search_result: Modelling other agents in open multiagent systems is widely regarded as an open research challenge. Recent work (e.g., Chandrasekaran et al. on I-POMDPs with open agent populations, and ongoing research on ad hoc teamwork and open ad hoc teamwork by Stone and collaborators) provides partial methods for special cases, but no general efficient method with the stated properties has been established.

status_evidence.title: Open Ad Hoc Teamwork using Graph-based Policy Learning
status_evidence.snippet: We consider the problem of cooperating with previously unseen teammates in open environments where agents may enter or leave at any time.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of efficient modelling/cooperation in open multiagent systems remains an active research challenge with only partial solutions.

status_evidence.title: Individual planning in open and typed agent systems
status_evidence.snippet: We extend interactive POMDPs to open agent settings where the set of other agents changes over time.
status_evidence.claim: Existing approaches address restricted versions of the open multiagent modelling problem.
